title: fix(spec): make the declaration-parity ratchet able to fail on a spec row with no manifest component
body:
Part of #18407

Clause-②: no

## TL;DR

Regenerating `sdui.manifest.json` does **not** produce `object-tree`, and no pin bump would
change that — measured, byte-identically, below. What this PR lands is the other half of the
card: `check:react-declaration-parity` **can now fail** on a spec row whose block has no
manifest component. It goes red on `object-tree` today, and **that red is the deliverable, not
a mistake** — the repository-side cure is upstream in objectui and is named in the failure text.

⚠️ This PR is a draft on purpose. Landing it as-is puts a standing red on a required context
for every PR in the repo. See "What has to happen before this lands".

## Leg 1 — re-measured on fetched `origin/main` (7d0f911da9), independently

```
git show origin/main:sdui.manifest.json
  components                            57
  component NAMES containing "tree"     []        == zero, a reading
  LIT CONTROL, same parse, first 6 names read out:
    object-grid · list-view · object-form · embeddable-form ·
    object-master-detail-form · object-kanban
  LIT CONTROL, same parse, every name starting "object-":
    object-grid, object-form, object-master-detail-form, object-kanban,
    object-calendar, object-gantt, object-timeline, object-map,
    object-metric, object-chart, object-pivot
```

The parser reads names, so the zero is a reading and not a failed search.

The other half, re-measured in `objectstack-ai/objectui` at the pinned
`53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694` (`.objectui-sha`, untouched by this PR):
`packages/plugin-tree/src/index.tsx` registers the same renderer **twice** —
`ComponentRegistry.register('object-tree', …)` at line 34 and
`ComponentRegistry.register('tree', …)` at line 41. Both carry a `namespace`, neither carries a
tier. That checkout is **shallow** (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` answers `true`); the
pinned commit object is present, so every reading above is a blob read at a named commit, not a
windowed history query, and none of them needed the truncated history.

## Leg 2 — regeneration is a byte-identical no-op

`node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs` (the generator that writes the tracked artefact; the
repo's `pnpm sdui:manifest` is the browser route and needs a vendored objectui build) was run
against published `@object-ui/*` 17.6.0, the version the pinned commit declares:

```
→ installing @object-ui/* 17.6.0 ... → enumerating the registry (16 modules)...
✓ wrote sdui.manifest.json (57 components, 66910 bytes, sha256 49211fee7792…)
```

After the run, with `git add -A` performed FIRST and `git diff --cached` read after it, the
manifest was **not in the diff at all**:

```
git rev-parse :sdui.manifest.json            78f870e42fe9fec1e9fad2e17c48370d8eca2cbe   (index)
git hash-object sdui.manifest.json           78f870e42fe9fec1e9fad2e17c48370d8eca2cbe   (worktree)
git rev-parse origin/main:sdui.manifest.json 78f870e42fe9fec1e9fad2e17c48370d8eca2cbe
sha256sum sdui.manifest.json                 49211fee7792…  == scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json
```

The only thing the run changed was `generatedAt` in the provenance record, `2026-09-08` →
`2026-09-20`. The artefact is unchanged, so that record still describes it accurately; the
date-only churn was reverted and the tree is clean against `origin/main`. **Nothing in this PR
hand-edits a generated artefact, and nothing in it touches `.objectui-sha`.**

## Leg 3 — what decides it: registered, but not public

The gate's own words are "NO component in the manifest — **not registered or not public**".
Measured against the same published 17.6.0 install the generator used, it is the second:

```
getAllConfigs()     494 configs — NAMES containing "tree":
                    ["ui:tree-view","plugin-tree:object-tree","view:tree"]   (deduped)
getPublicConfigs()   57 configs — NAMES containing "tree": []
  LIT CONTROL getAllConfigs()    grid names: ui:grid, field:grid, plugin-grid:object-grid,
                                             view:grid, plugin-grid:import-wizard,
                                             plugin-dashboard:dashboard-grid
  LIT CONTROL getPublicConfigs() grid names: object-grid, grid
PUBLIC_BLOCKS        57 entries — NAMES containing "tree": []
getConfig('object-tree') -> registered=true  tier=undefined  namespace='plugin-tree'
                            inputs=['objectName','tree']
getConfig('tree')        -> registered=true  tier=undefined  namespace='view'
  LIT CONTROL getConfig('object-grid') -> registered=true tier=undefined
```

`PUBLIC_BLOCKS` has exactly 57 entries and the manifest has exactly 57 components — the public
tier IS the manifest. The file and the lines that decide it, all in objectui at the pinned sha:

| what | where | says |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the curated list | `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` **lines 26–117** | 57 tags, neither `'object-tree'` nor `'tree'` among them |
| path 1 into the contract | `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` **line 821** | `for (const tag of PUBLIC_BLOCKS) add(tag, this.getContractConfig(tag));` |
| path 2 into the contract | `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` **line 824** | `if (cfg.tier === 'public' && !key.includes(':')) add(key, cfg);` |
| why neither path fires | `packages/plugin-tree/src/index.tsx` **lines 34–39 / 41–46** | both registrations pass `namespace` + `label` + `category` + `inputs`, and no `tier` |

⇒ Both producers — the node generator and the browser dump — faithfully serialize a registry
that genuinely does not expose `object-tree` on the public tier. The artefact is correct. The
divergence is that a spec row expects a component the public tier does not carry. This
reproduces, independently, the measurement the `domain:spec` seat recorded on the card.

## What this PR changes

`check:react-declaration-parity` could not fail on its loudest signal. The baseline ratchet
suppressed the `missing` axis behind

```ts
if (state.missing && base && !base.missing) regressions.push(…)
```

With no baseline row there is no `base`, so a spec row whose block the public registry does not
carry arrived **pre-accepted**: the gate printed its `✗` line and exited 0, and would have kept
doing so for as long as nobody regenerated the baseline. Measured on `origin/main` before the
change — the same run `lint.yml` performs on every PR:

```
✗ object-tree: NO component in the manifest — not registered or not public.
Summary: 126 spec-only divergences, 1 blocks missing from the registry.
## Baseline ratchet
✓ no new DECLARATION divergence vs accepted baseline
  exit 0
```

…while the very same gate in plain `--strict` mode (no baseline) already exits **1** on that
same tree. The teeth existed; only the mode CI actually runs swallowed them.

The asymmetry is what makes this a bug rather than a policy: `registryOnly` was **already**
ratcheted against an absent baseline row — `baseRO` falls back to the empty set, so every
registry-only input on an unbaselined block reports as new. Only `missing` carried the extra
conjunct. (The comment sitting under that loop, "a brand-new block … is fine (purely additive
coverage)", was therefore not true of the code it described.)

So:

- **`missing` is judged every run, baseline or not.** A `missing: true` baseline row does not
  buy silence either.
- **`--update` refuses to write a baseline while any block is missing**, naming the block. That
  is deliberate: `--update` is the one command that can mint an acceptance, and re-running it to
  clear a fresh red is the reflex this gate has to survive. The row it would write is exactly
  the `missing: true` the #18305 round declined to write, in that round's own words "that would
  be **accepting** a divergence rather than reporting it" — so the producer refuses rather than
  the reviewer having to remember.
- **The failure text carries the cure and rules the baseline out**: expose the block on the
  registry public tier (`PUBLIC_BLOCKS`, or `tier: 'public'` on the registration) and regenerate
  with `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`, or drop the spec row. ⛔ Never a baseline row.

⛔ No `missing: true` baseline row is added by this PR, and `packages/spec/react-declaration-parity.baseline.json` is not touched.

### The fixtures were resting on the hole

The exit-code fixtures in `check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.test.ts` fed the gate a
**one-component** manifest, so twelve of the thirteen evaluated blocks were absent from every
one of them — including the control that claims "exits 0 when the manifest matches the accepted
baseline". They passed only because an absent, unbaselined block could not regress. They now
declare every evaluated block, with the roster read off the gate's **own report** rather than
restated (a literal list would rot the day a `ComponentPropsMap` row lands), and `omit` spells
out the absence where an absence IS the subject.

### Reverse verification — both legs, on-disk proof, restored byte-identically

Run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, from the committed state, so the red/green numbers
are trustworthy and the restore has a real restore point:

| leg | mutation | on-disk proof | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A | put `&& base && !base.missing` back | anchor 1 → 0, blob `8bda7e2d5e7f` → `d4bf6f71d12a` | **3 failed / 33 passed** — exactly the three pins of the new red; every control stayed green, and the harness reproduced the hole verbatim (`✗ object-grid: NO component in the manifest` followed by `✓ no new DECLARATION divergence`) |
| B | neutralise the `--update` refusal predicate | anchor 1 → 0, blob `8bda7e2d5e7f` → `d81336b2a156` | **1 failed / 35 passed** — only the `--update` pin; the "still writes when nothing is missing" control stayed green |

Both restored with `blob == HEAD (8bda7e2d5e7f)` and `git diff HEAD` empty. No ablation
artefact is left in the tree.

## Checks — real exit codes

| check | exit | note |
|:--|:--:|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | **0** | required before any of the below is believable |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | **0** | includes `check:scripts-typecheck`, which compiles both changed files |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | **0** | 500 files / 14649 tests passed |
| `check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.test.ts` alone | **0** | 36 passed (30 before, +6 new) |
| `eslint . --no-inline-config` (the whole repo, not narrowed) | **0** | 6914 files linted, 0 files with findings — read from `--format json` |
| **`check:react-declaration-parity --baseline … --strict`** | **1** | ⚠️ **RED, and intended** — see below |
| 53 further derived gate families | **0** | derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `49f7e0d23e`, then run; list and logs in the report comment |
| `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` | 3 | each prints `PREREQUISITE NOT MET … NOT a pass: nothing was measured` — they read a full `pnpm build` closure. NOT MEASURED, not findings |
| `check:pm-dispatch-gates` | 124 | NOT MEASURED: its self-test exceeds a 9-minute foreground budget on this shared box. Whole-tree family; this diff does not touch `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` |

The red, in full:

```
## Baseline ratchet
⚠ NEW declaration divergence vs accepted baseline:
    - object-tree: declared in the spec, NO component in the manifest, and NO baseline row
      — so nothing here could have "regressed". The absence IS the divergence; it is not
      onboarding slack.

  → NO COMPONENT IN THE MANIFEST is a different class and has NO --update escape: the spec
    declares a block the public registry does not expose, so there is no prop-level
    disagreement to accept. Expose it on the PUBLIC tier (objectui `PUBLIC_BLOCKS`, or
    `tier: 'public'` on the registration) and regenerate — `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`
    — or drop the spec row. ⛔ Never a baseline row: that accepts the divergence instead of
    reporting it.
```

**Blast radius is exactly one block.** Of the thirteen blocks this gate evaluates, four have no
baseline row (`object-gantt`, `object-map`, `object-timeline`, `object-tree` — the committed
baseline's last write predates #18403, which added those `ComponentPropsMap` rows), and only
`object-tree` is absent from the manifest. The other three are present and stay green.

## What has to happen before this lands

`Lint & Repo Gates` is a required context, so merging this while `object-tree` has no manifest
component puts a standing red in front of every PR in the repo. Two routes, neither of which is
this seat's to pick:

1. **objectui first.** Add `'object-tree'` to `PUBLIC_BLOCKS` (or `tier: 'public'` on the
   `plugin-tree` registration), release, bump `.objectui-sha`, regenerate the manifest — then
   this PR is green and lands with it. That is the shape AGENTS.md already prescribes for a
   change that breaks against the pinned sibling: it ships together with the sibling fix and the
   pin bump, or it does not ship. ⛔ `.objectui-sha` is held by open PR #18723, so this seat did
   not touch it; and note a pin bump alone would **not** help — the pinned SOURCE lacks the entry
   too, measured above.
2. **spec side.** Drop the `object-tree` row from `ComponentPropsMap`, so the spec stops
   declaring a block the public tier does not carry. That reverses one arm of the decision landed in
   #18403, and is not a seat's call.

⛔ Deliberately **not** offered as a third route: writing the `missing: true` baseline row. The
#18305 round declined to write one for a stated reason, and this PR makes that refusal
mechanical rather than a matter of remembering.

## Acceptance notes

- `#17735` is a different cell on the same file (the tracked manifest vs the browser dump
  disagreeing on the fields the parity gate consults) and is out of scope here — it is not
  addressed by this PR and remains open. The relevant half was measured only incidentally: both
  producers agree about `object-tree`, because both read `getPublicConfigs()`.
- `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` carries a `generatedAt` that is now older than the last
  run which reproduced the artefact byte-for-byte. Noted, not filed: nothing reads that field,
  and re-recording a date under an unchanged sha256 is churn on a generated provenance record.
- No changeset. Measured rather than assumed: `@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]` is
  `dist, json-schema, liveness, prompts, llms.txt, README.md, src/**/*.zod.ts, CHANGELOG.md,
  api-surface, api-surface-declarations, spec-changes.json`; `packages/spec/scripts/**` is in
  none of them. Grepping every one of those paths after a build for `missingRegression`,
  `MISSING_IS_NEVER_RATCHETED_AWAY`, `fullManifestFor`, `evaluatedBlockTypes` and `stillMissing`
  returns **0 files each**, with positive controls `ComponentPropsMap` → 38 files and
  `PageComponentSchema` → 50 files on the same corpus. This diff publishes nothing, so it takes
  `skip-changeset`.
